title: Cap. 4 Mem. 2 close: Adversaries’ concessions; Gospel announceability to every nation
pass_a_gloss: Obj: even if pact blood-stabilized only for elect, remissio/salus may still be offered all under faith-hypothesis because elect will perseveringly believe — so no non-elect can charge pact false. Reply worthless: conditional proposition’s truth conceived before condition’s positing; even if condition never occurs, well-formed conditional must hold. Si-credideris remittentur false re Cain/Judas unless true connexion-ground if they believed. Parts’ separate truth/falsity irrelevant (Peter abnegaverit→life false though parts true; Peter non-crediderit→no life true though parts false). So Si-credideris→remission/life false re any non-elect (even never-to-believe) if antecedent connexion-cause lacking — lacking unless conditioned pact stabilized with all/each. Elect-only foedus does not entail ‘if Cain believes he is saved.’ Thus conditioned foedus stabilized with whole race. (3) From adversaries’ concessions (even maximum restrictors): merit of death = way for any unbeliever to escape deserved condemnation if he believes; death would abundantly suffice to save all if all believed; Gospel of crucified Christ announced indiscriminately elect/non-elect with promise all believers obtain remissio. Argue: if all would obtain remissio/salus if they believed → universal pact stabilized by death under faith-condition; antecedent true → consequent. Why: admitted conditional (Si tu credideris, whoever you are, salvus) not necessary by nature of thing (unlike fire→hot / man→animal) → truth founded in voluntary Divine ordination sanctioning consequent given antecedent for any human. No third foundation → Evangelical pact universal by God’s ordination, equally respects all/each. Obj: Gospel never announced to all → pact not for whole race. Reply: non-announcement ≠ non-sanction; what follows is: if not announceable in itself to nation/person → does not pertain. Other causes of non-announcement possible. Any age/nation/person could truly hear remissio in Redeemer’s death under faith — Job alien; Antipodes minister would not wait new stabilization. Paul: mystery hidden from ages now revealed (Col 1:26); stabilized from eternity with race though hidden/revealed as God pleased (Rom 16:25-26; Eph 3:5,9).
pass_b_english: But perhaps someone may say: Even if this pact stabilized by Christ’s blood pertains not promiscuously to all human beings but to the elect alone, yet remission and salvation can be proposed and offered to all under the hypothesis of faith, because it is certain that the elect alone will perseveringly believe; and therefore no one of the non-elect will ever be able to charge that this conditioned covenant was false on God’s part as to himself, or violated. But this reply is of no moment. For the truth of any conditional proposition is to be conceived before the positing of the condition: indeed, although the condition is never going to come into act, still the truth of a rightly instituted conditional proposition ought to stand. Here, then, the conditional proposition or promise, If you have believed, your sins will be remitted to you, is false as to Cain or Judas unless a true foundation of the connexion is given, if it should happen that they believe. Nor does it matter at all to the truth of a conditioned proposition whether they are going to believe or not; since in such a proposition the ratio of the connexion is looked to, not the truth or falsity of the parts taken separately. If Peter shall have denied Christ, he will obtain eternal life, is a false proposition because of the weakness of the connexion, and yet each part separately was true. If Peter shall not have believed, he will not obtain eternal life, is a true proposition, and yet each part taken apart was false: for Peter both believed and obtained eternal life. By like reason, then, this conditional pronouncement, If you have believed, you will obtain remission of sins and eternal life, would be false as to any non-elect person, even if he is supposed never going to believe, if the antecedent ratio and cause of the connexion is lacking: but it is lacking unless that conditioned pact is asserted stabilized with all and each human being. For it does not follow: God in Christ’s death sanctioned a covenant concerning saving all the elect by faith: Therefore if Cain shall have believed, he will be saved. That conditioned covenant is therefore stabilized with the whole human race.

3. We prove that this Evangelical pact stabilized in Christ’s death, concerning giving salvation under the condition of faith, is universal, by urging this same reason further, and that from the concessions of those who seem to oppose us. Those therefore who try most of all to restrict Christ’s death nevertheless concede that by the merit of Christ’s death there is some way and ratio constituted by which any unbeliever can escape merited condemnation, namely if he believes. They concede that Christ’s death would abundantly have sufficed for saving all human beings, if as many human beings as are in the whole world believed in him. They concede finally that the word of the Gospel concerning Christ crucified is announced indiscriminately to elect and non-elect, and all are commanded to believe in him, with this promise added, that all believing in him will obtain remission of sins. These things posited, I argue thus: If as many human beings as are in the whole world would obtain remission of sins and salvation if they believed, then there is firmed by Christ’s death a universal pact concerning saving any human being under the aforesaid condition of faith: But the first is true: Therefore also the second. The reason of the consequence is this: Because that conditional which they admit as much as to non-elect as to elect — namely, If you have believed, whoever at length you are, you will be saved — does not have necessary truth from the nature of the thing, as these do, If there is fire, it is hot, or, If it is a human being, it is an animal: it remains therefore that it have its truth founded in some voluntary ordination of God, by which he himself sanctioned that as to any human being, the antecedent being posited in being, the consequent also would be posited. For no third foundation can be assigned on which the truth of the aforesaid conditional rests. Therefore it must be confessed that that Evangelical pact is universal from God’s own ordination, and looks equally to all and each human being.

If anyone here objects that the Gospel itself was never announced to all human beings, and therefore neither does that Evangelical pact embrace the whole human race, or pertain to all and each, I reply: it does not follow, The Evangelical pact is not announced to this nation, or to this singular human being, Therefore as to them it was not sanctioned or stabilized: But this rightly follows, The Evangelical pact is not of itself Announceable to this nation, or to this human being, Therefore it pertains to them in no way. For other causes of the Gospel’s not being announced can underlie, while we still confess it announceable to all; which causes it is not of the present design to search out. We say therefore that in any age, to any nation, and to any human being, remission of sins in the Redeemer’s death under the condition of faith could truly have been announced. So in the time of the Old Testament this covenant was revealed to Job the foreigner. So in our age if an Evangelical Minister came to the Antipodes, he would not wait for a new stabilization of this conditioned covenant as to them, but at once, acknowledging it as stabilized, would announce it to them. And hence it is that the Apostle calls this word of the Gospel a mystery hidden from ages and generations, but now made manifest, and so on ([[Colossians 1:26 >> Bible:Colossians 1:26]]). He therefore acknowledged it stabilized from eternity with the human race, although hidden or made manifest to these or those according to the Divine good pleasure. See ([[Romans 16:25–26 >> Bible:Romans 16:25]]) and ([[Ephesians 3:5 >> Bible:Ephesians 3:5]]) and 9.

3. Probamus hoc Evangelicum pactum in morte Christi stabilitum, de danda salute sub conditione fidei, esse universale, hanc ipsam rationem ulterius urgendo, idque ex concessis illorum qui videntur nobis adversari. Qui igitur mortem Christi vel maxime restringere conantur, concedunt tamen, merito mortis Christi esse viam aliquam et rationem constitutam, per quam quilibet infidelis possit meritam condemnationem evadere, nimirum si credat. Concedunt, mortem Christi abunde suffecturam ad servandos omnes homines, si quotquot sunt in toto orbe homines in eum crederent. Concedunt denique, indiscriminatim electis et non-electis verbum Evangelii de Christo crucifixo annunciari, omnesque in ipsum credere juberi, addita hac promissione, Fore ut omnes in ipsum credentes remissionem peccatorum consequantur. Hisce positis sic arguo: Si quotquot sunt in toto orbe homines, consequerentur remissionem peccatorum et salutem, si crederent, tum est firmatum Christi morte pactum universale de servando quolibet homine sub praedicta fidei conditione: At verum primum: Ergo et secundum. Ratio consequentiae haec est; Quia illa conditionalis, quam admittunt tam quoad non-electos quam electos, nempe, Si tu credideris, quisquis tandem es, salvus erit, non habet veritatem necessariam ex rei natura, sicut ista, Si ignis est, calidus est, vel, Si est homo, est animal: relinquitur ergo ut habeat veritatem suam fundatam in aliqua voluntaria Dei ordinatione, qua ipse sanxit ut quoad quemvis hominem, posito in esse antecedente, poneretur et consequens. Nullum siquidem tertium fundamentum assignari potest, quo nitatur praedictae conditionalis veritas. Ergo fatendum est, pactum illud Evangelicum esse universale ex ordinatione ipsius Dei, et ad omnes ac singulos homines ex aequo spectare.

Si quis hic objiciat, ipsum Evangelium nunquam fuisse omnibus hominibus annunciatum, ac proinde neque pactum illud Evangelicum totum humanum genus complecti, vel ad omnes et singulos pertinere, respondeo; non sequi, Pactum Evangelicum non annunciatur huic nationi, aut huic homini singulari, Ergo quoad eos non fuit sancitum aut stabilitum: Sed illud recte sequitur, Pactum Evangelicum non est ex se Annunciabile huic nationi, aut huic homini, Ergo ad eos nullo modo pertinet. Causae siquidem non annunciati Evangelii aliae subesse possunt, ut illud omnibus annunciabile fateamur; quas causas rimari non est praesentis instituti. Dicimus igitur, quovis saeculo, cuivis nationi, et cuivis homini vere annunciari potuisse remissionem peccatorum in morte redemptoris, sub fidei conditione. Sic tempore Veteris Testamenti Jobo alienigenae fuit revelatum hoc foedus. Sic nostro saeculo si Minister Evangelicus ad Antipodas veniret, non exspectaret quoad eos hujus conditionati foederis novam stabilitionem, sed illico pro stabilito agnoscens iisdem annunciaret. Atque hinc est quod Apostolus hunc sermonem Evangelii vocat mysterium absconditum a saeculis et aetatibus, nunc autem patefactum, etc. Col. i. 26. Agnovit igitur ab aeterno stabilitum cum humano genere, quamvis absconditum sive patefactum hisce aut illis pro beneplacito Divino. Vide Rom. xvi. 25, 26 et Eph. iii. 5 et 9.
